standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma constructing, from a cardinal kappa, a subcomplex of a given complex of O-modules of size at most max(kappa, -) containing prescribed subsets of the terms
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies, at each step of the induction, the subcomplex of bounded size containing the chosen subsets of the groups of sections.

core_obligations: Choose representatives of the cohomology (proof lines 11247-11258): for every degree i and every object U pick a subset of the kernel of the differential mapping bijectively onto H^i(K)(U); its size is at most |K| because K can be represented by a complex of size |K|.

Produce the first subcomplex (proof lines 11258-11261): the cited building lemma yields a subcomplex S^bullet of F^bullet of size at most max(kappa, |K|) containing all the chosen subsets, so that H^i(S^bullet) -> H^i(F^bullet) is surjective on sections over every object.

Set up the induction (proof lines 11263-11276): one constructs subcomplexes S^bullet = S_0^bullet in S_1^bullet in ... of F^bullet, all of size at most max(kappa, |K|), with the property that the kernel of H^i(S_n^bullet) -> H^i(F^bullet) equals the kernel of H^i(S_n^bullet) -> H^i(S_{n+1}^bullet); the union H^bullet of the chain is then the required representative of size at most max(kappa, |K|).

Induction step (proof lines 11278-11293): for each U and i choose a subset of F^{i-1}(U) mapping bijectively onto S_n^i(U) intersect the image of the differential; it is again of size at most |K| because S_n^i(U) is bounded, and applying the building lemma to the union of these subsets with S^i(U) produces S_{n+1}^bullet with the required kernel property.
proof_roadmap: Pick subsets of the groups of sections representing all cohomology classes and bound their size by the size of the object.
Use the building lemma to obtain a first subcomplex of bounded size on which every cohomology class is visible.
Build an increasing chain of subcomplexes of bounded size whose kernels of the comparison maps stabilize, and take its union.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, in the situation of the chapter, a cardinal kappa such that every complex of O-modules representing an object K of D(O) contains a subcomplex representing K whose size is at most max(kappa, |K|) (statement lines 11237-11245). The proof (proof lines 11247-11293) first kills all cohomology classes by one bounded subcomplex, then builds an increasing chain of bounded subcomplexes whose comparison kernels stabilize, and takes the union. H2: a cardinal-bounded inductive construction with two inputs, written out in full.
